title: The Fox and the Crow (മലയാളം)
summary: In a quiet grove beside an olive press, a black crow perched upon a high branch, holding in his yellow beak a large wedge of savory sheep... [ML]
full_text:
In a quiet grove beside an olive press, a black crow perched upon a high branch, holding in his yellow beak a large wedge of savory sheep's cheese which he had carried off from a dairy window. As he prepared to enjoy his breakfast, a hungry red fox trotted by and caught the pungent aroma of the cheese.

Looking up into the boughs, the fox realized that he could neither climb the smooth trunk nor shake the branch. Sitting on his haunches, the fox tilted his head and spoke with honeyed sweetness: 'O noble monarch of the air! How radiant are your feathers in the morning sun! Surely the eagle himself cannot match the gloss of your ebony wings, nor the peacock the grace of your noble posture.'

The crow looked down, flattered by the praise, yet kept his beak firmly clenched around the cheese.

The fox sighed with theatrical admiration: 'If your voice is but half as sweet as your plumage is magnificent, you must surely be the undisputed king of all songbirds! How I long to hear a single melody from that royal throat, that I may bow before you as your humble servant.'

Drunk with pride and eager to prove his musical majesty, the foolish crow stretched his neck, flapped his wings, and opened his beak wide to let out a loud, grating: 'Caw! Caw!'

The moment his beak parted, the heavy cheese slipped from his grasp and tumbled straight down through the branches. The fox caught it neatly in his jaws before it touched the earth, swallowed it with relish, and smiled up at the crow: 'Thank you for the delicious cheese, my fine singer! In return, let me give you a piece of advice worth more than a basket of cheese: Never trust a flatterer, for he lives entirely at the expense of those who listen to him!'
moral: Flattery is the food of fools; he who listens to sweet falsehoods will surely lose his prize. [ML]
